transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting stuck on these thoughts at work. I’m a designer, so I deal with layouts and versions and files all day, and lately I keep having this nagging feeling that I’ve missed some tiny mistake—like a spacing issue, or the wrong logo, or I sent the client the wrong version of something.

And the frustrating thing is, a lot of the time I can look at it and know, logically, it’s probably fine. Like, I can see the file is correct, or I remember checking it. But then my mind just circles back to it anyway, like, “What if you missed something?” or “What if that wasn’t the final version?” It’s not huge, exactly, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Do these thoughts cause you a lot of anxiety or distress that's hard to manage, even when you know they might not make sense?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s like full panic every time, but it definitely gets under my skin and it’s hard to let go of. The thing that bothers me is that I can be looking right at the layout, and I can see the spacing is fine, the logo is the right one, the file name looks correct, whatever it is—and still this thought comes back like, “But what if you missed something tiny?” or “What if that wasn’t actually the right version you sent?”

And then I feel this pressure in my chest, or just this unsettled feeling, like I can’t quite move on cleanly. It’s not that I truly believe there’s always a mistake, because part of me knows I checked it. But my mind keeps circling back to it anyway, and it’s frustrating because it makes something that should be simple feel… sticky, I guess. Like the thought won’t resolve just because I know it probably doesn’t make sense.

When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking the files over and over, mentally reviewing what you did, or trying to get reassurance from someone—to try to feel more certain or reduce the discomfort?

Yeah… I do. That’s probably the part that made me realize it wasn’t just “being careful” anymore.

Before I submit something now, I’ll re-open the file even if I literally just had it open. I’ll zoom in, check the spacing again, compare the layers, make sure the right logo is on, make sure I didn’t accidentally hide or move something. Then I’ll sometimes re-save it, even though I know I already saved it, just because it feels like… I don’t know, like it locks it in somehow.

And then even after that, I’ll mentally walk through the whole thing again, like, “Okay, I chose that type size because of this, that image is the approved one, that version is the final one, the export settings were right.” It’s not like I’m spending my entire day doing only that, but it definitely slows me down. Something I used to submit and move on from now has this extra loop attached to it.

I don’t always ask someone else to check, because I don’t want to seem annoying or like I can’t do my job, but I do end up checking myself more than I need to. And creatively it makes me feel less free, honestly, because instead of just trusting my eye or making decisions and moving forward, I get kind of stuck proving to myself that everything is okay.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports intrusive, unwanted thoughts about potential mistakes, accompanied by repetitive behaviors (e.g., checking files repeatedly) and mental acts (e.g., reviewing decisions) aimed at reducing distress or preventing a feared event. These symptoms are consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The patient also demonstrates insight into the excessiveness of the behavior, which supports F42.9 (obsessive-compulsive disorder, unspecified). Other candidates like F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) and F32.9 (major depressive disorder, unspecified) are ruled out due to the presence of clear obsessive and compulsive features rather than generalized worry or primary depressive symptoms.
